function: Best-beam-index prediction (top-k) from fused radar and LiDAR data with a multimodal transformer (MMT), to cut the pilot overhead of BS beam selection (pp. 5, 9-10).
system: Downlink; BS with 16-antenna 60 GHz mmWave array, 64-beam codebook, single-antenna vehicle, co-mounted 4-antenna FMCW radar and LiDAR; no RIS (pp. 3, 10).
method: Multimodal transformer (MMT) classifier with feature-level radar-LiDAR fusion (image stitching or merging), trained supervised with cross-entropy loss; beam pruning from beam-index statistics (pp. 8-11).
data_channel: Real-world DeepSense 6G measured dataset, Scenario 31: 2,546 samples of radar and LiDAR frames with optimal-beam labels; 80% training, 20% testing (pp. 10, 12).
test_conditions: Single Scenario 31; 80% of 2,546 samples for training, 20% for testing; training set reduced to 10-100% in a data-size study; no other scenario tested (p. 12).
baselines: Learned: CNN with three conv and two FC layers, two kernel sizes (p. 11). MMT variants: LiDAR-only, first fusion only, merging versus stitching (p. 10). No non-learned method.
metrics: Top-k beam prediction accuracy (k=1 to 5); throughput in bps/Hz versus number of beam candidates; number of correctly predicted optimal beams after pruning; latency and FLOPs (pp. 10-12).
complexity: FLOPs: first fusion 4.16e7, second fusion 5.54e4, MMT 1.68e9, total about 1e9; average latency 8.3 ms; CNN of [18] quoted at 1e6 FLOPs (p. 12, Table 3).
q1_support: p. 10: "evaluated assuming the real-world DeepSense 6G dataset" (Scenario No. 31, measured data).
q2_support: p. 12: "are used for training, and the remaining 20% of samples" (reserved for testing); p. 10: "we present the results specifically for Scenario" No. 31. Only a held-out part of the same scenario is tested; no other scenario, site or configuration.
q3_support: p. 11: "proposed MMT with the performance of the CNN having" three conv layers is the learned baseline; p. 10: "only the point cloud from LiDAR is assumed as a baseline" is an MMT variant. No non-learned method (such as exhaustive beam search) is compared.
q4_support: p. 12: "TABLE 3. Latency and complexity (FLOPS) of data processing steps." and "average data processing latency of 8.3 ms was obtained."
q5_support: p. 10: "evaluated assuming the real-world DeepSense 6G dataset" (public dataset [8]); the authors give no link to their own code.
notes: PDF title and DOI match (p. 1). Tables 1 to 3 and Figs. 10 to 15 were read from the page images of pp. 10-12. Area 3 chosen because the learned MMT only selects the communication beam and the radar and LiDAR are separate sensors; the authors frame the work as ISAC (p. 1, special issue), so the reviewer may prefer area 5. The vehicle has one antenna but the BS has 16, so the system rule does not exclude it. Table 3 prints the total as about 1e9 FLOPs while the MMT row alone shows 1.68e9.
